sources.details: 0.5·1+0.5·0=0.5·0+0.5·1=0.5 exactly. An 8×48 real matrix has rank≤8 and kernel dimension≥40; adding a fixed bias cannot restore distinctions along its kernel. This is about unrestricted input differences, not an empirical task-accuracy claim.

claims.statement: Each patch is processed by the same trainable affine layer, using weighted sums plus bias; each weight row supplies one output.
claims.scope: nn.Linear(48,8) applies one weight matrix to the last axis of every patch; it does not mix patch positions or give dimensions predefined color meaning.

evidence.supports: y=xA^T+b, weight(8,48), bias(8), preserved leading dimensions and learnable parameters.
The same projection E applies to each patch.
Direct affine equality and identical-input identical-output; no cross-position mixing, available gradients and zero updates.

claims.statement: The exact fence receives (1,16,48), returns (1,16,8), and stores weights (8,48).
claims.scope: Default scene is one RGB 16×16 image and patch_size=4; 16 patch positions survive while the final width changes; this is a forward demonstration.

evidence.supports: Default image and patch count/48-value layout.
Only the last feature axis changes and weight is (out,in).
All three original printed shapes.
Direct slice checks for all16×48 patch values and manual affine equality.
